NEPHROLOGY NOTE   Date: 2026-10-17
32M, ambulatory visit for a scheduled nephrology problem evaluation.

S:
Patient presents for routine nephrology follow-up. He reports low energy and intermittent ankle swelling that worsens toward the end of the day. He has been following the low-sodium plan and taking medications as prescribed. He works as a dock loader. He could not complete 8 of his scheduled shifts last month because of symptoms. He also raises ongoing concerns about pain-medication use and asks about options for support. Sister with schizophrenia. Sleep is variable. Lives with a cousin who helps with rides. Never smoker, no alcohol.

O:
BP 132/84, HR 78, RR 16, Temp 98.1 F, SpO2 98% on room air. Weight 188 lb, up 2 lb from prior.
General: tired appearing, in no acute distress.
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no rub.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Extremities: trace bilateral ankle edema.
Psych: cooperative, linear thought process, engaged in discussion of goals.
Labs (this week): creatinine 2.6 mg/dL, eGFR 22 mL/min/1.73m2, potassium 4.8 mmol/L, bicarbonate 20 mmol/L, phosphorus 4.4 mg/dL. Urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio 360 mg/g.

A/P:
1. Chronic kidney disease stage 4, eGFR 22, followed by nephrology. Labs reviewed with patient. Continue ACE inhibitor with potassium monitoring. Reinforced low-sodium, moderate-protein diet; dietitian referral updated. Discussed long-term planning and education on future treatment options.
2. Opioid abuse, uncomplicated, discussed treatment options. Reviewed counseling and medication-assisted treatment pathways and provided a referral with the patient's agreement. Reviewed safe disposal of unused pain medication and provided naloxone education.
3. Function and work: symptoms are affecting his ability to keep regular shifts. Provided a letter describing current limits for his employer.

Repeat labs in 6 weeks. Return to clinic in 3 months, sooner for worsening swelling.
